name: Schedule
description:
Run prompts on a schedule. The plugin adds the ScheduleCronCreate, ScheduleCronList, ScheduleCronDelete and ScheduleCronReschedule tools, and the `/loop` and `/schedule` commands. The model schedules a task from usual words, for example "remind me at 3pm" or "every 5 minutes check the deploy". A heartbeat examines the tasks each second. It sends the prompt of each due task between turns through the `prompt.inject` port. The tasks are stored for each session at `~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<sid>.cron.json`.

On `--resume`, the tasks come back, but not a task after its time limit. To disable the plugin, set `MINIMAL_AGENT_DISABLE_CRON=1`.

tool.name: CronCreate
tool.description: Schedule a prompt to run on a cron schedule or at an interval. Use it to do a task after a time. Use it also to examine a deploy or a pull request until it is stable. To show or cancel a task, use `ScheduleCronList` or `ScheduleCronDelete`. Do not schedule a push, a delete or a deploy unless the user approved it. The tool gives the new task with its id, schedule and next fire time.

prompt.description: Necessary. The prompt to run at each fire. It goes into the session as a user turn, between turns, not during a response.

cron.description: A standard 5-field cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) in local time. You can use `*`, ranges (`1-5`), steps (`*/15`) and sets (`1,15,30`). For example, `0 9 * * 1-5` is 9 AM on weekdays. Give this value or `every`.

every.description: An interval, for example `5m`, `2h`, `1d` or `2 hours`. The tool changes an interval of one minute or more to a cron schedule, and adjusts it to a cron step. Give this value or `cron`.

recurs.description: The default is `true`. Set `false` for a one-time task, which the tool deletes after it fires. The maximum is 50 tasks for each session. A task that runs again stops after 7 days.

tool.name: CronList
tool.description: Show the scheduled tasks of this session, for example before you cancel or change one. To change a task, use `ScheduleCronReschedule` or `ScheduleCronDelete`. The tool gives the id, schedule, next fire time and prompt of each task.

tool.name: CronDelete
tool.description: Cancel a scheduled task with its 8-character id, when the task is complete or the user does not want it. To change the fire time, use `ScheduleCronReschedule`. The tool gives the removed id and the number of tasks that stay.

tool.name: CronReschedule
tool.description: Change the next fire time of a scheduled task. Use it to set a new interval, or to move a one-time task to a different time. To make a task, use `ScheduleCronCreate`. The tool gives the task id, the new interval and the next fire time.

every.description: A new interval for all subsequent fires, for example `30s`, `5m` or `2h`. Give this or `nextAtMs`.

nextAtMs.description: A Unix time in milliseconds for one next fire. Then the task goes back to its schedule. Give this value or `every`.

commands.name: loop
commands.summary: Run a prompt on repeat while the session is open

commands.name: schedule
commands.summary: Schedule a prompt by cron, or list/cancel tasks
